name: ids
description: Identifiers and encodings: ULID, KSUID, nanoid, Snowflake, UUID v4/v7 from bytes, base58, base62, base36, base32 and Crockford

api.name: base58_alphabet
api.doc: The base58 alphabet of Bitcoin addresses: digits and letters without `0`, `O`, `I` and `l`.

api.name: base62_alphabet
api.doc: The base62 alphabet: `0-9`, `A-Z`, `a-z`, in that order (as KSUID and most base62 libraries).

api.name: base36_alphabet
api.doc: The base36 alphabet: `0-9` then `a-z`.

api.name: crockford_alphabet
api.doc: Douglas Crockford's base32 alphabet: `0-9` and the letters without `I`, `L`, `O` and `U`.

api.name: encode_base
api.sig: fn encode_base(b: Bytes, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2) -> Str
api.doc:
The bytes `b` written in the base of `alphabet` (its length), most significant digit first:
the bytes are one big-endian number, and every leading zero byte becomes one leading copy of
the alphabet's first character, as in Bitcoin's base58, so `decode_base` gives the same bytes
back. Empty bytes give `""`.

api.name: decode_base
api.sig: fn decode_base(s: Str, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2) -> Opt[Bytes]
api.doc:
The bytes that `encode_base` wrote as `s`, or `none` if `s` has a character outside the
alphabet. Each leading first character is a zero byte.

api.name: encode_int
api.sig: fn encode_int(n: Int where _ >= 0, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2) -> Str
api.doc:
The non-negative integer `n` in the base of `alphabet`, without leading zeros (`0` is the
alphabet's first character).

api.name: decode_int
api.sig: fn decode_int(s: Str, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The integer `s` spells in the base of `alphabet`, or `none` for `""`, a character outside the
alphabet, or a value above the 64-bit maximum. Leading zero digits are allowed.

api.name: encode_big
api.sig: fn encode_big(n: BigInt, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2) -> Str
api.doc: The non-negative `BigInt` `n` in the base of `alphabet`, without leading zeros.

api.name: decode_big
api.sig: fn decode_big(s: Str, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2) -> Opt[BigInt]
api.doc:
The `BigInt` `s` spells in the base of `alphabet`, or `none` for `""` or a character outside
the alphabet.

api.name: base58
api.doc: Bitcoin base58 of `b` (`encode_base` with `base58_alphabet`).

api.name: from_base58
api.doc: The bytes of Bitcoin base58 text, or `none`.

api.name: base62
api.doc: Base62 of `b` (`encode_base` with `base62_alphabet`).

api.name: from_base62
api.doc: The bytes of base62 text, or `none`.

api.name: base36
api.doc: Base36 of `b` (`encode_base` with `base36_alphabet`, lower case).

api.name: from_base36
api.doc: The bytes of base36 text, either case, or `none`.

api.name: base32
api.sig: fn base32(b: Bytes, pad: Bool) -> Str
api.doc: RFC 4648 base32 of `b` (`A-Z`, `2-7`), padded with `=` to a multiple of 8 characters when `pad`.

api.name: from_base32
api.doc:
The bytes of RFC 4648 base32 text, either case, with or without padding (padding, when
present, must make the length a multiple of 8). `none` for other characters, an impossible
length, or nonzero unused bits.

api.name: crockford
api.sig: fn crockford(n: Int where _ >= 0, check: Bool) -> Str
api.doc:
The non-negative integer `n` in Crockford base32 (upper case, no leading zeros), followed by
the mod 37 check symbol (`0-9A-Z` without `ILOU`, then `*~$=U`) when `check`.

api.name: from_crockford
api.sig: fn from_crockford(s: Str, check: Bool) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The integer of Crockford base32 text: either case, hyphens ignored, `I` and `L` read as `1`
and `O` as `0`; with `check`, the last character must be the right check symbol. `none` for
anything else or a value above the 64-bit maximum.

api.name: ulid_from
api.sig: fn ulid_from(ms: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 281474976710655, rnd: Bytes) -> Str
api.doc:
The ULID of a Unix time in milliseconds and 10 random bytes: 26 Crockford base32 characters, the
48-bit time first, so ULIDs sort by time as text.

api.name: parse_ulid
api.doc:
The 16 bytes of a ULID, or `none` unless `s` is 26 Crockford base32 characters (either case,
no `I`, `L`, `O` or `U`) starting with `0` to `7` (higher values exceed 128 bits).

api.name: is_ulid
api.doc: Whether `s` is a ULID (`parse_ulid`).

api.name: ulid_time
api.doc: The Unix time in milliseconds of a ULID, or `none` if `s` is not one.

api.name: ulid
api.doc: A new ULID from the clock and 10 random bytes from the operating system.

api.name: UlidGen
api.sig: pub type UlidGen = {last_ms: Int, last_rand: Bytes} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The state of a monotonic ULID generator: the time and random part of the last ULID.

api.name: ulid_gen
api.doc: A monotonic generator that has made no ULID yet.

api.name: ulid_next
api.sig: fn ulid_next(g: UlidGen, ms: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 281474976710655, rnd: Bytes) -> Opt[(Str, UlidGen)]
api.doc:
The next ULID of a monotonic generator and its new state, as the ULID specification describes:
a later millisecond uses `rnd`; the same millisecond, or an earlier one (a clock that went
back), keeps the last time and adds 1 to the last random part, so every ULID sorts after the one
before. `none` when the random part would overflow (2^80 ULIDs in one millisecond).

api.name: ulid_next_now
api.sig: fn ulid_next_now(g: UlidGen) -> Opt[(Str, UlidGen)] ! time, rand
api.doc: `ulid_next` with the clock and fresh random bytes.

api.name: ulid_to_uuid
api.doc: The UUID text of the same 128 bits as a ULID, or `none` if `s` is not one.

api.name: ulid_from_uuid
api.doc: The ULID of the same 128 bits as a UUID, or `none` if `u` is not a canonical UUID.

api.name: ksuid_epoch
api.doc: The KSUID epoch, 1400000000 seconds after the Unix epoch (2014-05-13T16:53:20Z).

api.name: ksuid_from_epoch
api.sig: fn ksuid_from_epoch(secs: Int, epoch: Int, rnd: Bytes) -> Str
api.doc:
The KSUID of a Unix time in seconds and 16 random bytes, counting time from `epoch` (Unix
seconds): a 32-bit time then the random bytes, as 27 base62 characters that sort by time.

api.name: ksuid_from
api.sig: fn ksuid_from(secs: Int, rnd: Bytes) -> Str
api.doc:
The KSUID of a Unix time in seconds (from 2014-05-13 to 2150) and 16 random bytes, with the
standard epoch.

api.name: parse_ksuid
api.doc:
The 20 bytes of a KSUID, or `none` unless `s` is 27 base62 characters of at most 160 bits
(`aWgEPTl1tmebfsQzFP4bxwgy80V` is the largest).

api.name: is_ksuid
api.doc: Whether `s` is a KSUID (`parse_ksuid`).

api.name: ksuid_time_epoch
api.sig: fn ksuid_time_epoch(s: Str, epoch: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The Unix time in seconds of a KSUID made with `epoch`, or `none` if `s` is not one.

api.name: ksuid_time
api.doc: The Unix time in seconds of a KSUID with the standard epoch, or `none` if `s` is not one.

api.name: ksuid
api.doc: A new KSUID from the clock and 16 random bytes from the operating system.

api.name: nanoid_alphabet
api.doc: The alphabet of nanoid's default ids: 64 URL-safe characters (`A-Za-z0-9_-`).

api.name: nanoid_from
api.sig: fn nanoid_from(rnd: Bytes, alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2 and _.len <= 256, size: Int where _ >= 0) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The id nanoid's algorithm makes from the random bytes `rnd`: each byte, masked to the smallest
`2^k - 1` that covers the alphabet, picks a character when it falls inside the alphabet and is
skipped otherwise, so every character is equally likely. `none` when `rnd` runs out before
`size` characters. The bytes are used in order (nanoid's JavaScript reads them from the end).

api.name: nanoid_custom
api.sig: fn nanoid_custom(alphabet: Str where _.len >= 2 and _.len <= 256, size: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str ! rand
api.doc:
A random id of `size` characters from `alphabet`, by nanoid's unbiased algorithm, with bytes
from the operating system. It draws `ceil(1.6 * mask * size / len)` bytes at a time (nanoid's
step) until it has enough; after 64 draws, which happens with a probability below 2^-64, it
fills the rest by taking bytes modulo the alphabet length.

api.name: nanoid
api.doc: A nanoid: 21 characters from `nanoid_alphabet`, about 126 random bits.

api.name: short_id
api.sig: fn short_id(size: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str ! rand
api.doc:
A random id of `size` letters and digits (`base62_alphabet`), for ids that must not contain `-`
or `_`. Eight characters carry about 47 bits; use 22 or more for unguessable ids.

api.name: Snowflake
api.sig: pub type Snowflake = {epoch_ms: Int, time_bits: Int, node_bits: Int, seq_bits: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The layout of Snowflake-style 64-bit ids: milliseconds since `epoch_ms` in the top `time_bits`,
then a node (machine or shard) number in `node_bits`, then a per-millisecond sequence in
`seq_bits`; the three add up to 63 so ids are positive `Int`s.

api.name: SnowflakeParts
api.sig: pub type SnowflakeParts = {ms: Int, node: Int, seq: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The parts of a Snowflake id: Unix time in milliseconds, node and sequence.

api.name: twitter_layout
api.doc: Twitter's layout: epoch 1288834974657 (2010-11-04), 41 time bits, 10 node bits, 12 sequence bits.

api.name: snowflake_layout
api.sig: fn snowflake_layout(epoch_ms: Int, time_bits: Int, node_bits: Int, seq_bits: Int) -> Opt[Snowflake]
api.doc:
A layout with an epoch of your own and the usual 41, 10 and 12 bits; `none` unless the bit
counts are non-negative and add up to 63.

api.name: snowflake_compose
api.sig: fn snowflake_compose(l: Snowflake, p: SnowflakeParts) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The id of `p` in layout `l`, or `none` when the time is before the epoch or any part does not
fit its bits.

api.name: snowflake_decompose
api.sig: fn snowflake_decompose(l: Snowflake, id: Int where _ >= 0) -> SnowflakeParts
api.doc: The parts of the id `id` in layout `l` (the time as Unix milliseconds).

api.name: SnowflakeGen
api.sig: pub type SnowflakeGen = {last_ms: Int, last_seq: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The state of a Snowflake generator: the millisecond and sequence of its last id.

api.name: snowflake_gen
api.doc: A Snowflake generator that has made no id yet.

api.name: snowflake_next
api.sig: fn snowflake_next(l: Snowflake, g: SnowflakeGen, node: Int, at_ms: Int) -> Opt[(Int, SnowflakeGen)]
api.doc:
The next id of node `node` at Unix time `at_ms`, and the new state: a later millisecond starts
the sequence at 0; the same one, or an earlier one (a clock that went back), keeps the last time
and adds 1 to the sequence, so ids only grow. `none` when the sequence is full (wait for the
next millisecond and call again) or a part does not fit the layout.

api.name: uuid_from_bytes
api.doc: The canonical lower-case text of 16 bytes as a UUID, or `none` for another length.

api.name: uuid_bytes
api.doc: The 16 bytes of a canonical UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex digits, either case), or `none`.

api.name: uuid_v4_from
api.doc:
The version 4 (random) UUID of 16 random bytes: their version bits set to 4 and variant bits to
RFC 9562's, as `uuid.v4()` does with bytes from the operating system.

api.name: uuid_v7_from
api.sig: fn uuid_v7_from(ms: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 281474976710655, rnd: Bytes) -> Str
api.doc:
The version 7 (time-ordered) UUID of a Unix time in milliseconds and 10 random bytes: the 48-bit
time, version 7, 12 random bits, the variant, 62 random bits (RFC 9562 section 5.7). The first
random byte gives its low 4 bits and the third its low 6.

api.name: uuid_v7_time
api.doc: The Unix time in milliseconds of a version 7 UUID, or `none` if `s` is not one.

api.name: nil_uuid
api.doc: The nil UUID, all zeros.

api.name: max_uuid
api.doc: The max UUID, all ones.
